title.narrative: Integrated Education and WASH interventions for returnees and communities in areas of origin enabling safe and dignified returns in Aleppo and Deir-ez-Zor (Priority – Envelope 2)

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtDespite over 1.14 million Syrians returning to their Areas of Origin by May 2025, significant barriers persist, including extensive infrastructure damage (shelter, education, WASH), critical lack of basic services, pervasive protection risks, and widespread economic insecurity. The proposed action will contribute to addressing these challenges while aligning with ltbgtSHF 2025 First Standard Allocation Strategy priorities under Envelope 2lt/bgt supporting safe and dignified returns through an area-based integrated intervention aiming to enhance well-being and equitable access to Education and WASH services for returnees and communities in Areas of Origin in subdistricts of Daret Azza and Atareb in Aleppo governorate and subdistricts of Ashara and Deir-ez-Zor city in Deir-ez-Zor. ltbrgtThe intervention strategy is structured also to strength ltbgtcommunity-based protection via a Child Protection (CP) referral mechanismlt/bgt in Non-Formal Education (NFE) centers as well as to cross-cut GBV, PSEA prevention and community engagement approaches throughout the whole action. ltbrgtThe project design leverages lessons, best practices and community feedback from prior SHF-funded WWGVC interventions (2023-2024). Target Area of Intervention selection aligns with ongoing activities and LHF prioritization (underserved, newly accessible and hard-to-reach areas with high severity of needs and vulnerabilities), informed by WWGVC's ltbgtMay 2025 Need assessment (Annex 1)lt/bgt. ltbrgtltbgtltugtEducation Componentlt/ugt: lt/bgtltbrgtThis component will increase access to safe, quality, protective education for ltbgt4,146 people acrosslt/bgt 7 communities in Aleppo and Deir-ez-Zor: ltbgtHameidiyyeh, Quriyeh , Kafr Taal, Oweijel, Tadil , Bala and Balentalt/bgt. Activities include: ltbrgtLight rehabilitation of 56 classrooms (3 schools), including 6 gender and disability-inclusive WASH facilities. ltbrgtProvision of solar-powered systems and school furniture. ltbrgtActivation of NFE programs (FLN and RCs) for 1,000 children (550 girls 450 boys). ltbrgtProvision of 7 recreational kits to schools. ltbrgtProfessional development for 100 NFE and FE teachers (around 85 women, 15 men) on protective and inclusive teaching, plus NFE teacher coaching/mentoring. ltbrgtCommunity engagement through 21 PTA meetings in NFE-supported schools. ltbrgtDevelopment of 20 recreational events at community level. ltbrgtltbgtltugtWASH Componentlt/ugtlt/bgt: ltbrgtThis component will improve access to safe, reliable, and sustainable WASH services for ltbgt4 targeted communities (Hameidiyyeh, Quriyeh , Kafr Taal, Oweijeland)lt/bgt and schools under the Education component, promoting a safe learning environment. ltbrgtltbgtAleppolt/bgt: Rehabilitation of the full water system (pumping station, reservoir, distribution network) in Kafr Taal solarization of the water pumping station and rehabilitation of water networks in Oweijel technical assessment of borehole conditions. ltbrgtltbgtDeir-ez-Zorlt/bgt: Rehabilitation of water networks in Quriyeh and Hameidiyyeh rehabilitation of the sewage network in Hameidiyyeh. ltbrgtltbgtBoth Governorates:lt/bgt Provision of tools/equipment to local Water Board Units (WBs) and municipalities for facility maintenance/management workshops/training for Water entities members. ltbrgtThe WASH outcome reach ltbgt25,383 individuals (13,534 females and 11,849 maleslt/bgt).lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtltbgtThe integrated responselt/bgt across both sectors targets the same priority subdistricts and beneficiaries based on needs. It complements other WWGVC interventions (ECHO/AICS/UNDP-funded) to maximize impact. Coordination with stakeholders (MoE, WB, WASH, Education sectors) was assured (Annex 9 Endorsement Letters). lt/pgtltpgtCentral to design, implementation, and monitoring is the focus on ltbgtProtection and AAPlt/bgt, ensuring safety, inclusion, and dignity while addressing specific and intersectional needs. Systematic MEAL activities will detect/mitigate protection risks and gather feedback to adapt the response.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtOverall, the project targets ltbgt26,929 individuals (29% returnees, 71% communitieslt/bgt ltbgtin Areas of Origin)lt/bgt comprising ltbgt53% female and 47% malelt/bgt, including at least ltbgt10% People with Disabilitieslt/bgt (PwD). lt/pgt
